    How the map is made

    The city detail is real Miami. Vice City is Rockstar's take on Miami, so the streets, freeways and buildings you see when you zoom in are real-world data from OpenStreetMap (© OpenStreetMap contributors, ODbL). Rockstar's streets differ; pins sit in the district a guide names, not on an exact in-game doorstep.

    The shape is a stand-in. Leonida is Rockstar's version of Florida, so the outline is the real Florida coastline (Natural Earth, public domain) drawn in neon, with the far panhandle trimmed and Lake Okeechobee standing in for Lake Leonida. It is not Rockstar's map art and it is not to scale with the game.

    The pins are from written guides. Each spot comes from a guide linked on its card, with the date we read it. Reported means a named gaming outlet said it; Unverified means only fan sites did. The ring around a pin shows how sure the position is: small for a named town or district, wide when only the region is known.

    The labels match the rest of the site. Reported means a named outlet said it. Tested means we did it ourselves on the game version shown. When Rockstar releases an update, older spots get a warning until someone re-checks them.

    Want the exact map? Rockstar's own Leonida map is a free download on the GTA VI site. Use it next to this one.
